title: Mixed-dialogue residency emulation & continuous-batcher tuning
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: production workloads show a mix of very short prompts with long streaming responses (customer chat) and long multi-turn prompts with short completions (dev tools). Continuous-batcher currently coalesces by arrival time and soft length buckets; however we observe frequent KV-cache eviction churn, uneven GPU slab utilization, and widened p99 latency tail when a small fraction of requests are long-lived.

Goal: implement a runtime-level 'KV residency emulation' combined with a length-stratified continuous-batcher tuning strategy to reduce eviction churn, improve GPU memory packing, and stabilize p99 latency for mixed prompt/response workloads without regressing throughput. This ticket covers design, simulator experiments, implementation prototype, and gradual rollout behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: p99 token latency for mixed-production trace reduced by >=20% compared to baseline on canary hosts
KV eviction churn (evictions/min) decreased by >=30% for mixed-dialogue load in simulator and canary tests
End-to-end tokens/sec change within +/-5% of baseline under typical traffic
No customer-facing errors introduced during feature-flag rollout; fallback to legacy batching path works within 10s
Configuration knobs (residency window, soft-reserve percentage, preemption-timeout) exposed and documented
technical_notes: Residency emulation: instead of hard-reserving fixed KV slots (costly), maintain a probabilistic soft-reservation token per request that increases 'residency score' for KV entries produced by that request. Eviction policy will bias against entries with high residency score for a tunable window (ms).

Length stratification: incoming requests are placed into three logical lanes (fast/medium/long) based on estimated total sequence length (prompt + expected response). The continuous-batcher favors filling fast+medium lanes for low-latency SLOs while allowing long lane to accumulate larger batches for throughput efficiency.

Soft preemption: implement cooperative preemption where a long-running stream can be signalled to yield next-slot at a pacing boundary if the runtime detects impending GPU memory pressure; the stream then re-enqueues with elevated residency score to avoid immediate eviction of its KV entries.

Memory-pressure simulator: we will build a lightweight offline simulator that replays production arrival traces (token-by-token timing) and models KV residency scores, eviction decisions, GPU slab utilization, and batching packing. Use simulator to sweep residency-window, soft-reserve percentage, and preemption timeout to find Pareto points.

Metrics to add: kv_residency_score_distribution, kv_evictions_per_min, kv_hit_ratio_by_age, batch_fill_factor_by_lane, p50/p95/p99_token_latency_by_lane, gpu_slab_fragmentation_percent, preemption_signals_rate

Backward compatibility: runtime switches between legacy eviction (LRU-like) and residency-emulation eviction. Ensure kv indexing/versioning is unchanged; only eviction heuristics change. Feature flag must be per-cluster and per-model.
Data needed: three 48h production traces tagged by customer type (chat-heavy, dev-tool-heavy, balanced) for simulator. Obtain via internal trace-store query T-2026-03-09-01.
